articles.title: IAF’s Fighter Jet Revolution: AI, Digital Twins & 3D Printing | 930 Indian Firms Join Push| News18
articles.description: The Indian Air Force is transforming how it maintains its fighter fleet, turning to artificial intelligence, digital twins, predictive analytics and 3D printing to keep aircraft operational amid persistent spare-parts challenges. The IAF is now working with 930 Indian firms, including private companies and MSMEs, to strengthen indigenous maintenance capabilities.The drive has already resulted in around 62,300 indigenised aircraft spares, saving an estimated ₹582 crore in foreign exchange over the past five years. Locally produced components now account for around 97% of the spares most frequently drawn by operational units and 93% of mandatory spares needed for overhauling decentralised fleets.The IAF has also been using an in-house 3D additive manufacturing facility since 2022 to produce certain urgent, low-volume components. At the same time, digital twin technology, AI and predictive analytics are helping technical crews move from reactive repairs to predictive maintenance, allowing potential faults to be identified before they cause operational failures.The effort covers major fleets including the Su-30MKI, Rafale, Tejas, Mirage 2000, MiG-29 and Jaguar.
